questions.scenario: A school locker gets broken into. How do you find out who did it?

options.text: Look for physical clues like a scuff mark, a shoe print, or a dropped pen left behind by the culprit.
Check the school's Wi-Fi router logs to see which student's phone connected near that hallway at the time of the break-in.
Analyze a weird sticky substance left on the locker handle to figure out if it's glue, gum, or some kind of chemical.
Think about who has a grudge against the student and observe suspects to see who is acting nervously today.

questions.scenario: You are watching a detective thriller movie. What part makes you lean forward in your seat?

options.text: When they tape off the room, put on gloves, and meticulously bag every single piece of evidence.
When they hack into a suspect's encrypted laptop to recover deleted chat history and secret files.
When the lab tech runs a complex test and discovers a rare, untraceable poison in the victim's tea.
When the detective interrogates the suspect, trying to break their lies by reading their subtle body language.

questions.scenario: You find a mysterious locked metal box buried deep in your backyard. What is your first move?

options.text: Dust the outside for old fingerprints and carefully pry the lock open without damaging it.
Take a picture of the serial number and search the deep web to find out its exact manufacturing origin.
Carefully swab the rust and dirt on the outside to test what kind of soil or chemicals it was exposed to.
Think about the history of your house and try to profile what kind of person would bury something here.

questions.scenario: In a social deduction game like 'Among Us' or 'Mafia', what is your primary strategy to catch the bad guy?

options.text: Tracking everyone's exact physical locations and paths on the map to see who crossed the crime scene.
Staring at the security cameras, admin logs, and task bars to catch a technical lie in someone's alibi.
Running a specific 'test' (like watching someone do a visual task) to get undeniable, foolproof evidence.
Listening to how people defend themselves and catching the subtle panic or over-explaining in their voice.

questions.scenario: What kind of puzzles or challenges do you naturally enjoy the most?

options.text: Jigsaw puzzles where I have to physically piece together broken fragments to see the big picture.
Logic puzzles, coding challenges, or deciphering secret encrypted messages.
Chemistry sets or science experiments where I figure out what hidden ingredients are reacting.
Riddles about human behavior, motives, and complex 'who-dunnit' mysteries.

questions.scenario: Your sibling is lying to your parents about where they went last night. How do you silently know they are lying?

options.text: I notice red mud on their shoes that only comes from a specific park across town.
I casually sneak a look at their phone's location history or recent Wi-Fi connections.
I can smell a specific perfume, smoke, or restaurant food on their jacket that gives them away.
I watch their eyes darting around and notice they rehearsed their story a little too perfectly.

questions.scenario: If you could have one super-spy gadget, which one would you choose?

options.text: A pair of glasses that instantly highlights invisible fingerprints and footprints in glowing colors.
A specialized USB drive that can instantly bypass passwords and download any phone's hidden data.
A pocket scanner that instantly identifies any liquid, drug, or chemical composition it touches.
A smartwatch that tracks a person's heart rate and alerts you the exact moment they tell a lie.

questions.scenario: What is your biggest pet peeve when people tell stories?

options.text: When they leave out the physical details (like what the room looked like or what time it was exactly).
When they exaggerate facts that can easily be disproven by a quick Google search.
When they make up unscientific nonsense that breaks the basic laws of biology or chemistry.
When the actions of the people in the story make absolutely no psychological or logical sense.

questions.scenario: You are assigned a huge school project on a famous true crime case. What angle do you choose to present?

options.text: The timeline of how the physical evidence was found, collected, and preserved at the scene.
How the police used cell phone tower pings and deleted text messages to track the criminal.
The detailed scientific breakdown of the rare toxic substance used, and how it affected the body.
The childhood background of the criminal and the psychological factors that drove them to do it.

questions.scenario: What is your favorite way to observe the world when you are bored?

options.text: Looking at tire tracks, shoe prints, or tiny objects left on the ground and wondering where they came from.
Thinking about how everything is connected through networks, hidden cameras, and digital footprints.
Wondering about what things are made of at a chemical level—ingredients, compounds, and reactions.
People-watching in a cafe or park, guessing their relationships, moods, and what secrets they hide.

Crime_Scene_Investigator.title: Crime Scene Investigator (CSI)
Crime_Scene_Investigator.primary_match_text: You are highly observant, hands-on, and detail-oriented. You love being in the field and finding physical clues that everyone else overlooks.
Crime_Scene_Investigator.day_in_the_life: Arriving at a cordoned-off crime scene, photographing evidence, dusting for fingerprints, and carefully bagging hair or blood samples without contaminating them.
Crime_Scene_Investigator.alternative_match_text: Because you are so observant and meticulous, roles in Law Enforcement (Detective) or Forensic Anthropology are also fantastic fits for you.
Crime_Scene_Investigator.roadmap: Take Science (PCB or PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Forensic Science, followed by specific training at police academies or specialized institutes.

Digital_Forensic_Analyst.title: Digital Forensic Analyst / Cyber Investigator
Digital_Forensic_Analyst.primary_match_text: You are tech-savvy, highly logical, and a natural puzzle-solver. You thrive in the digital realm, cracking codes and tracing digital footprints.
Digital_Forensic_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Recovering deleted files from a suspect's seized phone, tracing illegal cryptocurrency transactions, and finding the true IP address of a cyber-attacker.
Digital_Forensic_Analyst.alternative_match_text: With your strong technical skills and logic, becoming an Ethical Hacker (Penetration Tester) or Cybersecurity Expert is a highly lucrative alternative.
Digital_Forensic_Analyst.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Computer Science, Cyber Security, or a B.Sc in Digital Forensics.

Forensic_Toxicologist.title: Forensic Toxicologist / Chemist
Forensic_Toxicologist.primary_match_text: You are detail-oriented, scientific, and laboratory-focused. You love chemistry, biology, and using science to figure out what hidden substances are at play.
Forensic_Toxicologist.day_in_the_life: Running complex blood and tissue tests in a high-tech lab to find out if a victim was poisoned, or exactly what drugs were in a dangerous driver's system.
Forensic_Toxicologist.alternative_match_text: Since you love chemical analysis and lab work, careers as an Analytical Chemist, Pharmacologist, or Clinical Pathologist are perfect backup plans.
Forensic_Toxicologist.roadmap: Take Science (PCB or PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Chemistry, Biochemistry, or Forensic Science, followed by a Master's (M.Sc) in Toxicology.

Forensic_Psychologist.title: Forensic Psychologist / Criminal Profiler
Forensic_Psychologist.primary_match_text: You are empathetic, deeply analytical, and fascinated by human behavior. You want to understand *why* people do terrible things, not just *how*.
Forensic_Psychologist.day_in_the_life: Interviewing criminals in prison to understand their motives, testifying in court about a suspect's mental state, or helping police build a profile of an unknown serial offender.
Forensic_Psychologist.alternative_match_text: Because you are fascinated by the human mind, Clinical Psychology, Criminology, or becoming an Interrogation Specialist are excellent parallel paths.
Forensic_Psychologist.roadmap: Take Arts/Humanities (with Psychology) or Science in 11th/12th. Pursue a BA/B.Sc in Psychology, followed by an MA/M.Sc in Forensic or Clinical Psychology.
